SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Pin Oak Energy Partners Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-01-27
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 874814
Permit API: 039-25764
Unconventional: Yes
County: Crawford
Municipality: East Fallowfield Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-01-27
Comments: Inspection related to cleanup of brine and oil inside the liner which is used as secondary containment for the stock tank (old frac tank); see photo 1. The tank has overflowed/over-sprayed from a thief hatch or access door. A Pin Oak Energy employee and two-man crew from Diamond Energy Partners has vac-trucked brine/oil from the liner. Some oil/paraffin and brine still remains in the liner. During the cleanup, brine has leaked out of a hole in the bottom of the liner and flowed onto the soil-cement stabilized limestone pad. As of Monday, 1/27/20, some of the affected limestone has been placed in a roll-off on site. Clean up will continue on 1/28/20 to remove contaminated material from under the liner, and correct the secondary containment issues. Contaminated material on the well pad needs removed/remediated. Also, all contamination needs removed from within the secondary containment. SWMA violations noted for discharge of residual waste (brine) to ground. Site restoration violations are also cited in this Notice of Violation. The well site has not been restored to post-construction stage.

Comments: On November 21, 2024, the Department conducted a restoration inspection of the Diamond 3 OG Well in Nicholson Township, Fayette County. The inspection was conducted in response to a Well Site Restoration Report received on 7/25/2024.The following was observed:The well was reported to be plugged without a monument present. The access road appears to be unrestored at the time of this inspection. The Department requests that the Operator restore the access road or provide the Department with the following information if it is to remain.1. Map of the area being proposed to remain including if there would PCSM proposed in that area.2. Map or overlay of how the site was to be restored.3. Include property boundaries.4. Or documentation that the access road is pre-existing. The erosion and Sedimentation Control Plan and Well Control and Disposal Plan were on site. Temporary E and S Controls were not installed at the time of this inspection, in accordance with the E and S Plan. The completion of plugging for this well reportedly occurred on 3/13/2024 therefore the well site shall be restored no later than 12/12/2024 per current regulations.Based on today's inspection, the WSRR is not approved. Violations shall be issued for failure to have the site temporarily stabilized and failure to implement E and S plan.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/27/2025 to CNX GAS CO LLC in East Finley Township, Washington county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CNX GAS CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/27/2025
Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8214920
Permit API: 125-28510
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: East Finley Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/27/2025
Comments: On 12/27/2024 an Incident Response inspection was conducted the MOR42 Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 12/27/2024 CNX Resources Representative, Ben Geary, reported an approximately 40-gallon brine release off containment at the MOR42 Well Pad located in East Finley Township, Washington County.CNX Resources representative, Ben Geary, and SPSI representative, Mac Maydak, were on site at time of inspection. Mr. Geary informed the Department that that the release was discovered on Saturday, January 25 at 1:15 pm, that the quantity released was approximately 40 gallons, and that a contractor (SPSI) had been dispatched the same day. Mr. Maydak stated that his crew was dispatched on Saturday (1/25) at approximately 1:40 pm. The origin of the release was stated to be a crack found on a T-joint along a line connecting to a slug catcher to the production tanks, which could be observed in front of the Unit H Gas Processing Unit (GPU).Mr. Geary stated that remediation efforts had taken place Saturday (1/25), Sunday (1/26), and continued into today (1/27). The area remediated at the time of inspection measured approximately 38 by 18 feet and to a depth of 1 inch, excluding the sump created on the western side of the GPU that measured approximately 8 inches in depth. It was made known that field screening was conducted during the remediation efforts with screening values between 2,000 and 12,000 s/cm observed. Mr. Maydak stated that 4 Vac boxes had been filled with removed material at the time of inspection.Mr. Geary stated that the remediation efforts would continue until all conductivity values were below 3,000 s/cm and that the sump would be monitored and any fluid that appears would be screened and removed via vac truck.PA DEP Conductivity probe calibrated on 12/27/2024.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo 1).-A crew was on site remediating near the Unit H GPU. A vac truck and vac box were observed near the remediation site (Photos 2-3).-The remediation area near the Unit H GPU and the source of the release were observed. A crack was observed on the T-joint of a line beneath a lock out-tag out tag. The lines appeared to be coated in a white film, obscuring visual observations (Photos 4-6).-The excavated areas located in front of and on the west side of the GPU were observed. It appeared that pad aggregate had been removed down to the larger riprap (Photos 7-8).-Field soil conductivity screening was conducted in various locations of the remediation site. The bottom and side walls of the sump were screened, with conductivity values ranging between1.682 ms/cm(1,682s/cm) and 4.71 ms/cm observed. Screening was conducted along the northern edge of the GPU and values of 2.56 ms/cm and 1.927 ms/cm (1,682s/cm) were observed. An area in front of the adjacent equipment on the western side of the GPU was screened. Values in this area ranged between 2.66 ms/cm and 11.69 ms/cm (Photos 9 -16).Determination:Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued for the release. A violation of 78a64a(a) is being issued for the lack of secondary containment.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 986952
Permit API: 081-21907
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cascade Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/03/2023
Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the Salt Run HC EXT Pad A location. Inspection accompanied by EQT Company Man Matt Casler and EQT Senior EHS Coordinator Zac Subra. Weather conditions at time of inspection are overcast and 38 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while the spill response is ongoing.According to the Emergency Response Notification Report submitted by EHS supervisor Rick Hall, 'approximately one barrel of production fluid was released to the pad surface off containment and approximately 50 barrels of production fluid were released on containment at the Salt Run Pad A Extension. EQT was in the middle of a frac on the pad when a pipe came apart and spilled the production fluid onto containment and soil. Tobias Machining and Welding was contracted to perform remediation worm on the impacted soils. No waterways or stormwater structures were impacted.'During site inspection and discussions with Mr. Subra and Mr. Casler, the following details were reported. Universal Pressure Pumping was conducting a zipper frac of four wells at the time of the incident. Violation ID: 977711
Permit API: 083-47206
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/07/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted upon being notified by Bull Run Resources that a crude oil release had occurred from a gathering line located at this well site.Upon my arrival on the well site, Eric Clancy of Bull Run explained that a pinhole formed in a steel gathering line located behind the location (east-northeast of the well, GPS coordinate 41.80141N 78.85587W). It appears that crude oil has been discharging from this pinhole at a minimal rate for an unknown period of time.Bull Run has repaired the failure in the gathering line, which has stopped the discharge. Oil soaked soil that was excavated to locate and repair the line remains staged on the well site. Crude oil traveled alongside the southeastern corner of the location for approximately 30 feet before reaching a roadside ditch that runs along the southern edge of the spur road. Evidence of crude oil was observed across an approximate 125 foot stretch of this ditch. Field screening with a PID meter did not detect appreciable VOC readings downslope of 41.80182N 78.85616W. Oil soaked leaves and a thin layer of oil soaked soil have been excavated from the southeastern perimeter of the well site and the ditch, this material is staged on the side of the road.Bull Run has constructed an underflow dam near the southern corner of the well site and has placed numerous absorbent pads on pockets of free crude that remain in the excavated area where the line was unearthed and in the ditch. I suggested to Eric that an additional underflow dam be constructed in the ditch downslope of the point where crude has thus far migrated as a preventive measure. Additional underflow dams and/or absorbent pads/booms should also be considered elsewhere across the impacted area to improve the initial containment efforts. Finally, Eric and I discussed the potential excavation of additional soil in the immediate vicinity of the gathering line, given the presence of visible product in this area. All methods of containment should be regularly monitored and maintained.At the time of this inspection, it is estimated that approximately 10 tons of oil soaked soil and leaf litter have been excavated and are in need of disposal. Additional soil excavation will likely be conducted throughout upcoming remediation activities. At this time, the evidence available suggests that less than one barrel of crude oil was released and no watercourses were impacted by this release.It is requested that Bull Run provide a remediation plan and keep the Department apprised of any developments that pertain to the cleanup of the remaining residual crude oil associated with this release. Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate remediation efforts and determine if additional measures are required.This well is a conventional well, equipped for production with a pump jack. A site ID sign is posted on the jack. The coordinates for this well were updated as part of this inspection.

Comments: I received notification from Oil and Gas Management regarding a public report of water being discharged from the Brown #1 well site, it was stated there was an odd smell, there was concern about if it was safe to be discharged. I arrived onsite and found a hose running down hill from a tank battery on Farm Lane that was used to hold presumed fresh water during the recent completion of this well. The well operator was draining the water tank and using it to water their freshly seeded and mulched areas. I used my conductivity probe and determined the water being discharged from the tank was not suitable to be dispersed to the ground as the conductance of the fluid was in excess of 16000S, which is above the allowable limit of 1000S. The operator immediately shut the valve and ceased the discharge. It is estimated over 1 barrel of fluid was released prior to closing the valve. Mr. Branch called to get additional equipment onsite to begin remediating the release. It was advised to get a vac truck for any standing water, and the mini excavator on site to begin soil removal.From the end of the discharge hose, the water ran approximately 35 feet in a westerly direction across a portion of the site, reaching an open earthen drainage ditch, this ditch connects to the local storm sewer somewhere along Crestview Blvd. Flowing water in the storm sewer was observed at the bottom of Crestview Blvd, due to lack of access I was unable to get my conductivity probe into the water to determine if it was from the Brown #1 site.

Municipality: Pleasant Township

Comments: I received notification from Oil and Gas Management regarding a public report of water being discharged from the Brown #1 well site, it was stated there was an odd smell, there was concern about if it was safe to be discharged. Comments: During a routine complete inspection on 5/16/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3788146), I noted API 065-26269 did not have a well tag, equipment not necessary for production was being stored on site, and there was evidence of a production fluid release greater than 42 gallons.During a follow up inspection (FUI) on 6/26/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3790440), I noted the well had a new well tag, the pipe was moved across the access road, and the spill area was seeded and mulched. The Department did not receive a response from the Notice of Violation with the operators intentions to use either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The Department did not receive tipping receipts or waste manifests associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from the spill. The tag violation was closed. The other violations remained open.On a FUI on 8/19/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3816085), I noted the Department still hasn't received tipping receipts or waste manifests regarding the clean up of this site. I emailed Ray Hepler information about Act 2 remediation. On 8/28/2024, Jack Crow, Henry Kramer, Brian Shank and myself met with Ray Hepler at the PA DEP Meadville Regional Office to discuss the outstanding violations at the Wheeler property. Ray Hepler stated he had the contaminated soil from the brine releases on a roll off and would send us the manifests soon. The Department received a manifest for waste on 9/9/2024. However, the manifest stated the soil was "Beaver-PA 100%". The manifest also stated the soil was hauled in a "white pick up truck", but during the 8/28/2024 meeting Ray Hepler stated the soil was in a roll off container. This manifest does not show the proper disposal of the soil from the Wheeler W12 well site located in Jefferson County. Today (9/12/2024), Brian Shank and I conducted a FUI. The pipe not necessary for production was still being stored near the access road. The spill area appeared to have new top soil and grass seed. We collected soil conductivity readings throughout the spill area. A background soil conductivity reading was collected. The soil conductivity reading was 154.5 pS/cm. Near the production tank, the soil conductivity reading was 3.28 mS/cm. Approximately 4 feet from the production tank, the soil conductivity reading 1416 pS/cm. These readings indicate that the prior spill has not been remediated yet. We collected grab soil samples to send to the Department's accredited laboratory. The samples will be analyzed for SAC 960 and UVIR.The outstanding violations for the Wheeler W12 well site will remain open at this time.

Comments: On July 11, 2023, inspection conducted at the Rumpelstiltskin well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. Present were myself, EQT representatives David Crayne and Carey Vallor-Bell, and Moody representative Jona Stoskey. This inspection was conducted in response to a spill that reportedly occurred on July 10, 2023 at 2:35 PM, and was reported to the Department the same day at 4:27 PM by DJ Hardy. The Department spoke over the phone with Mr. Hardy while en route to the pad, who explained that a GPU dumpline failed and spilled approximately one barrel of brine fluid onto the ground. He also stated that the area behind the unit was excavated, but impacted soil remains around and under it. The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP was onsite (see photo 2). The access road and well pad appeared to be stable with no evidence of accelerated erosion or sedimentation (see photos 3 and 4). GPU units were not placed in secondary containment (see photo 5). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. Soil conductivity readings were taken around the excavation, which read 2,360 and 2,750 Microsiemens (see photos 7 and 8). An additional conductivity reading was taken in what appeared to be a brine puddle at the bottom of the excavation, which read above the meter's range (see photo 9). A well tag was present on well 6H, with no observed leaks or discharge on the ground around it, and it appeared to be equipped for production (see photo 12). There are three other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 11). The Department recommends the operator replace the repaired portions of CFS.- CFS where the surface water exits the site appears to be failing, showing signs of overtopping and undercutting. The Department recommends the operator replace the current CFS and properly maintain CFS on site until restoration is achieved.- The absorbent pads that were left on site by the operator appear to remain on site at this time. Unconventional: No

Comments: On 3/14/2024 OGI Geoffrey Lutty conducted an onsite inspection of the Martin 2 gas well, API 129-27948. The well appeared equipped for production. The well displayed moderate corrosion. The well name and API was scratched into a pipe clamp, this does not meet the posting requirements of 3211(G). The line leading to the production tank appears to have failed and separated. A second tank was unused onsite as seen in the photographs, it is recommended to remove this equipment under OGA 3216(c). OGI used a Bascom Turner EGA 611 and detected multiple gas leaks. Gas was leaking from the base of the wellhead as seen in the attached photographs at 12%LEL. The line leading into the production tank appears to have separated and was leaking gas at 79%Gas. The soils in a 2' radius around the failed connected were tested and gas was detected at a peak of 31%LEL in the soils at 3" depth. No 2023 APR is on record, the latest record is from 2022 and indicates production. No 2023 MIA is on record, the latest record is from 2022. Based on todays inspection the following violations will be issued: OGA3211(G) - Failure to install permit number and operator information. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. 78.121(B) - Failure to electronically submit Annual Production Report to the Department. 78.88(d) - Failure to notify the Department and take corrective action to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion or other signs of deterioration that compromises the integrity of the well. 78.73(a) - Failure to operate the well in accordance with 25 PA code Chapter 78 and ensure the integrity of the well is maintained. 78.74 - Venting of gas to the atmosphere that produces a hazard to public health and safety.

The release was then reported to the DEP via the 24 hour number. Expand will begin remediation on 10/09/2025. The quantity of the release is unknown. The following reoccurring violations are cited against API #015-23861:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)Due to the unknown quantity of the release this will be referred to Act 2 for compliance. The following violations remain open against API #015-23861:CSL 402(b)35 P.S. 6018.301 SWMA25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)This case has been referred to the Environmental cleanups and Brownfields program and all violations will remain outstanding until results have been reviewed and compared to Act 2 standards by the ECB program, and an approval letter has been issued.I departed at 1125 hours.

He stated that the contaminated soil from the clean-up was added to the same truck containing soil from the southwest, and that he would eventually be providing tipping an manifest information. The outstanding violations for this well will remain open.

All associated violations discussed in both inspection reports are being issued/continued in just this inspection.A COA with the DEP was entered into on 3/07/2019. At this time, a rig was on site and plugging operations have commenced.During IRs 4157087/4157136/4157162, the DEP recommended the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan and redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.During IRs 4157480/4157532, the DEP recommended the operator install CFS along the access road in all sections of E and S off of the access road and above each culvert inlet and outlet, as well as gravel the access road at all culvert crossings in accordance with the E and S plan. The DEP recommended the operator install orange construction fence along the access road near the seep and wetland identified near the culvert 4 inlet and past culvert 5. The DEP recommended the operator restore the roadside ditch at seep.At the time of this inspection, the E and S plan was present in the on-site mailbox at the beginning of the access road. The DEP did not observed any redlining on site plans to depict and appropriately match on-site field changes (Photo 2). The DEP also did not observe the RCE to be installed at the beginning of the access road as depicted on the plans (Photo 1). The access road was also observed to still not be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plan calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary". CFS was observed to be installed at an area where erosion and sedimentation off the access road was previously noted to be located before culvert 1.Observations obtained during today's inspection at culvert crossings 1-5 are as follows:Culvert 1 crossing - culverted for a roadside ditch (Photos 4-7): The outlet still appears to be block. CFS was observed at both the inlet and outlet, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete surface contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert 2 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 8-9): Outlet still appears to be blocked. CFS was observed to be installed and functioning properly at both the inlet and outlet. Culvert 3 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 10-13): The inlet to this culvert appears to still be blocked. CFS was installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.Culvert 4 crossing - culverted for roadside ditch (Photos 14-17): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this culvert, however, the CFS at the inlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. Culvert still appears to not be receiving water due to operator disturbing channel and causing water to be diverted further down access road. The disturbed channel still appears to be carrying fine sediment towards the stream at culvert 5, however no sediment was observed entering the stream due to the second half of the channel going subsurface with the entry point into the stream unseen (Photos 18-20).Culvert 5 crossing - stream crossing (Photos 21-24): CFS was observed to be installed at both the inlet and outlet of this crossing, however, the CFS at the outlet is improperly installed as complete contact to the ground was not observed. No sediment was observed to be entering the stream at this time.

Comments: On 9/10/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Gergely 1 well in Munster Township, Cambria County.This inspection was conducted in response to a referral from OGI Matt Woods (Inspection ID: 4268198 on 9/01/2026; Inspection ID: 4269845 on 9/03/2026). OGI Matt Woods requested that a WQS follow up because of potential surface pollution concerns regarding a plastic-lined pit observed during IR 4269845.This inspection is not evaluating compliance with Order 450586, as it is being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- No equipment related to production and/or well plugging operations was observed on site. The plastic-lined pit documented in IR 4269845 was not observed during this inspection (Photos 11 and 19). No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site at the time of inspection. No plugging monument was observed at the former location of the well. The API number and Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) were found on site (Photos 16 and 17).- The access road and well site remain heavily rutted, which appears to be caused by vehicles and machinery that were tracked-in for well plugging operations. Some mulch and seed was observed on site. However, the mulch and seed implemented on site is inadequate, as large portions of exposed soil are observable (Photos 12-15 and 20-21).- No perimeter Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls were observed on site. No E and S Restoration plan was observed on site during this inspection.Based on today's inspection, the violations issued in IR 4263564 against the heavy tire rutting and for failure to have the E and S/Restoration plan available on site will remain outstanding. An additional violation is being issued in this inspection for failure to implement adequate seed and temporary stabilization on areas that were disturbed by well plugging operations.The outstanding violations issued for failure to post the API number and operator's information on site are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The Department requests that the Operator provide an electronic copy of the Control and Disposal Plan and provide clarification regarding the purpose of the plastic-lined pit observed during the time of IR 4269845, what it contained, and method of disposal used. Please provide this clarification no later than 9/29/2026. Additional violations may be forthcoming upon receipt and review of the clarification from the Operator.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Seneca Resources' DeCristo (01-128) D well site located in Sullivan Township, Tioga County on 11/10/2025 at 1020 hour. The weather was 29 degrees F with cloudy skies and light snow. An Act 9 sign, site plans and inspection log are located at the site entrance.A crew from "Force Flow" was conducting work on the wells onsite. Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8246798
Permit API: 051-24154
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Jefferson Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/27/2025
Comments: On August 27, 2025, the Department met on-site with the Operator and Moody and Associates to assess the access road culvert inlet. Accompanying me today is Lisa Raffle (Diversified), Glenn Wilson (Diversified), Jessie Bobrzynski (Moody), and Jona Stoskey (Moody).Due to the approximate specific conductivity threshold of 4.00 mS (according to Moody and Associates), the stained area observed in IR 4040776 on the access road will not be assessed. During today's on-site inspection/meeting, specific conductivity of the soil under the rip rap of the access road's culvert inlet was measured by the Department and Moody. Moody utilized their own specific conductivity probe/meter as well as a probe/meter supplied by Diversified. The Department utilized its own specific conductivity probe/meter. All three specific conductivity probes/meters were calibrated on-site prior to the inspection/meeting.Upon arrival to the culvert inlet, Lisa Raffle of Diversified informed the Department that she took readings of specific conductivity following the Department's latest on-site inspection (IR 4040776), to which she did not observe readings anywhere near as high as the Department did. The Department asked Raffle where the readings were taken from, to which Raffle indicated it was from the excavated area (Photo 2) within the culvert ditch. This small excavated area is observed to be upslope of the culvert and just downslope of the access road. The Department clarified that each of the specific conductivity readings for this inlet that were probed by the Department in previous on-site inspection were probed directly in front of the culvert inlet.Specific conductivity readings were probed by Moody and the Department in front of, under, and on the sides of the culvert inlet. Readings were observed to be 'Or' (Out of Range) or above 20.0 mS underneath and to the right (South) of the culvert. Glenn Wilson (Diversified) promptly removed approximately one and a half 5-gallon buckets of impacted material from this area (Photo 3).Following the removal of this material, Moody probed again and recorded readings between 6.0-10.0 mS underneath the culvert inlet. At this time, Diversified and Moody jointly decided to halt removal of material and collect a soil sample of the soil that was producing the 6.0-10.0 mS readings. The Department also collected a soil sample (SAC 960) from this location following Moody's collection. Based on today's inspection, all issued violations remain outstanding.
